headline: Digital Communications Manager at Connect Europe
about:
Political scientist holding a master's degree in Political and Social Communication with over ten years of experience working designing and implementing communication strategies, managing social media accounts, maintaining relations with the press and organising events.

Six years ago I decided to restart my professional career at the EU level in Brussels. I have always been interested in communicating European policies, which means a hard but motivating challenge.

currentPosition.description:
- Website: Daily liaison with our website agency to creatively and professionally maintain and improve the site. Coordinate with Media and Policy Teams to ensure all sections are current and engaging. Monitor analytics and suggest improvements over time.
- Social Media: Manage Twitter and LinkedIn to ensure lively, engaging, and professional content that amplifies policy messages and reaches key audiences.
- Newsletter: Produce internal and external newsletters, including the Daily Press Review, weekly #ConnectNews, and the Weekly Agenda.
- Events & Support: Work closely with comms and events teams to bring the Connect Europe brand to life across in-person, hybrid, and online events. Provide support on logistics, promotion, and ad hoc projects like webinars and seminars.
- New Projects: Contribute to developing a video content strategy and explore new social media platforms relevant to our audience.
- Rebranding: Led the rebranding from ETNO to Connect Europe. Managed collaboration with the branding agency, coordinated board and member input, and oversaw the website migration from Joomla to Drupal, including content, UX, and technical execution.

projects.title: European Youth Event 2014
projects.description:
European Youth Event 2014 (EYE) is organised by the European Parliament at the European Parliament's seat in Strasbourg from 9th to 11th May 2014. The EYE focuses on young people from the EU Member States, candidate states and neighbourhood countries aged between 16 and 30 years.

This event gives the opportunity to young Europeans to exchange perspectives and ideas in order to develop new solutions to the questions regarding the future of Europe. Furthermore, the event encourages the ongoing debate on the future of European policy issues in the run-up to the European elections and gives the young Europeans a platform to present their ideas on Europe to European political decision-makers for the new legislative period 2014-2019. The event will focus on five topics on the future of young Europeans: (1) Youth Unemployment, (2) Digital Revolution, (3) Future of the European Union, (4) Sustainability and (5) European Values.
